n482176d6f37.s: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of fertigation?
o: Control of the alkalinity of irrigation water
Increased availability of nutrients to plants
Reduction in the leaching of chemical nutrients
n482176d6f37.x: Fertigation helps control water alkalinity, raises nutrient availability and reduces leaching; efficient application of rock phosphate is not one of its advantages.

n4a2928313ed.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Micro Irrigation Fund (MIF)?
o: It is a Rs 10,000 crore corpus with NABARD
It was operationalised in 2015-16 along with Per Drop More Crop
It was set up with an initial Rs 5,000 crore
Another Rs 5,000 crore was added for the 15th Finance Commission period
n4a2928313ed.x: MIF was operationalised in 2019-20; it is Per Drop More Crop that began in 2015-16.

n17ab5d70f94.s:
Assertion (A): The AP Socio-Economic Survey 2024-25 records large-scale implementation of drip and sprinkler irrigation in the State.
Reason (R): The AP Socio-Economic Survey 2024-25 identifies precision farming, drones and IoT as key areas of focus.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n17ab5d70f94.x: Both are findings recorded in APSES 2024-25, but naming precision farming, drones and IoT as focus areas does not explain the existing large-scale drip and sprinkler coverage.

n5c2286830f5.s:
Assertion (A): Sprinkler irrigation generally suffers greater wind and evaporation losses than drip irrigation.
Reason (R): Sprinklers spray water through the air, whereas drip delivers water directly at the root zone.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n5c2286830f5.x: Because sprinkler water travels through the air it is exposed to wind and evaporation, while drip water is applied at the roots, so R explains A.

n7e79d210105.s: Which of the following pairs relating to the Digital Agriculture Mission is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Digital public infrastructure – Soil Fertility Profile
n7e79d210105.x: The mission's outlay is Rs 2,817 crore, not Rs 28,170 crore; it was approved in September 2024 and its DPI includes AgriStack, Krishi DSS and the Soil Fertility Profile.

n12bbb119e0f.s: Alternate wetting and drying in the System of Rice Intensification mainly reduces the emission of which gas from paddy fields?
n12bbb119e0f.x: Alternate wetting and drying avoids continuous flooding, cutting methane production from paddies; SRI also uses less seed and saves electricity on pumping.

n60a5f1e18f1.s: From 2022–23, Per Drop More Crop (PDMC) has been implemented under which scheme?
n60a5f1e18f1.x: PDMC, launched in 2015–16, was part of PMKSY up to 2021–22 and has been implemented under RKVY since 2022–23.

n002803afedc.s: Which centre, set up in 2012, runs ISRO's crop forecasting under FASAL?
n002803afedc.x: The Mahalanobis National Crop Forecast Centre (2012) runs ISRO's FASAL crop forecasting.

n86eca16073e.s: Which irrigation method has the highest water-use efficiency, about 90%?
n86eca16073e.x: Drip irrigation is about 90% efficient, sprinklers about 70–80% and flood or furrow irrigation about 30–50%.

ncee54429b4c.s: PMKSY, with the State Agriculture Department as nodal authority, is a:
ncee54429b4c.x: PMKSY is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme and the State Agriculture Department is its nodal authority.

nd720ee33e68.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about gene-drive mosquitoes?
o: A CRISPR-Cas9 gene drive copies itself onto the partner chromosome
Over 90% of offspring inherit the drive instead of the normal 50%
Population suppression aims to make the mosquito unable to support parasite development
'Transmission Zero' is a Tanzania-led project on GM mosquitoes
nd720ee33e68.x: This reverses the two types: population suppression uses sterile females, while population modification stops the parasite developing.

nbiology-43-6.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: GMO – Broad term for any organism whose genome is altered by genetic engineering
Purpose of a transgenic organism – Organism carrying a foreign gene from another species
Transgenic organism – Carries a foreign gene from another species
Transgenic crops – Biotechnology or agricultural application
nbiology-43-6.x: The purpose of a transgenic organism is a desired characteristic or product; carrying a foreign gene from another species is what defines the transgenic organism itself.

nebf05f31f8d.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Bt brinjal?
o: The GEAC recommended its release in 2009
It was developed through collaboration among Mahyco, UAS Dharwad and TNAU
Its principal target was the fruit and shoot borer
The moratorium on it was imposed in 2012
nebf05f31f8d.x: The moratorium on Bt brinjal was imposed in 2010 by Jairam Ramesh, not 2012; the other statements are correct.

nbiology-42-6.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about plasmids?
o: Some natural plasmid genes confer antibiotic resistance
Plasmids are usually linear, single-stranded DNA
Experimental plasmids are used as vectors
Plasmids are used to clone, transfer and manipulate genes
nbiology-42-6.x: Plasmids are usually circular, double-stranded DNA, not linear single-stranded DNA.

n78e2f188039.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about site-directed nuclease (SDN) gene editing categories in India?
o: SDN-1 makes a small change without a template or foreign DNA
SDN-2 uses a template and inserts foreign DNA
SDN-1 is exempt from GM rules under the 2022 guidelines
SDN-3 inserts foreign DNA and is regulated as GM
n78e2f188039.x: SDN-2 uses a template but introduces no foreign DNA, and it is also exempt under the 2022 guidelines.

n451d2d823c9.s:
Assertion (A): The Cartagena Protocol governs the transboundary movement of living modified organisms.
Reason (R): The Cartagena Protocol entered into force in 2003.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n451d2d823c9.x: Both are true: the Protocol (adopted 2000, in force 2003) governs transboundary movement of LMOs, but its date of entry into force does not explain its scope.

n2689252c1db.s:
Assertion (A): Reduced pesticide use is a claimed environmental benefit of Bt cotton.
Reason (R): Bt cotton carries a Bacillus thuringiensis gene that makes the plant produce its own insecticidal toxin.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n2689252c1db.x: Because Bt cotton makes its own insecticidal Bt toxin, less pesticide needs to be sprayed, so R explains A.

nf33d64d55fa.s:
Assertion (A): In the CRISPR-Cas9 system, the guide RNA acts as the molecular scissors.
Reason (R): In the CRISPR-Cas9 system, Cas9 cuts the DNA while the guide RNA acts as the navigator.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
nf33d64d55fa.x: Cas9 is the molecular scissors and guide RNA only leads it to the target, so A is false and R is true.

nbiology-39-3.s: Microbial production of useful products is an application of biotechnology in which field?
nbiology-39-3.x: In industry biotechnology gives microbial products; in agriculture GM crops, in medicine drugs and vaccines, and in research biochips.

n217548e9997.s: The Centre of Excellence for CRISPR Innovation and Translation (CoE-CIT) is to be set up in:
n217548e9997.x: The CoE-CIT is to be set up in Bengaluru.

n27cc8122ee0.s: The inactive Bt protoxin is activated in the gut of the insect larva because of its:
n27cc8122ee0.x: The protoxin is activated in the alkaline gut of the larva; the active toxin then binds midgut cells and creates pores.

nbiology-39-6.s: In biotechnology, the creation of a collection of genetic material is called a:
nbiology-39-6.x: A genetic library is a collection of genetic material; gene cloning copies a gene and biochips aid drug discovery.

n853d62562af.s: Which pest has developed resistance to the Bt toxins of Bt cotton?
n853d62562af.x: The pink bollworm has overcome Bt toxins; whitefly and mealybug are sucking pests whose numbers rose, a separate problem.

n552ab795a49.s: In recombinant DNA technology, which enzyme joins DNA fragments?
n552ab795a49.x: DNA ligase joins the fragments; restriction endonucleases cut DNA.

n6770d1d9c82.s: HTBt cotton combines the Bt trait with tolerance to which herbicide?
n6770d1d9c82.x: HTBt cotton combines glyphosate tolerance with the Bt trait; its approval in India is pending over weed-management and socio-economic concerns.

n72ad08b5445.shape: statements (one-liner not possible: every original item is correct)
n72ad08b5445.s:
Which of the following may be adversely affected by Bt toxins or other engineered traits?
1. Pollinators and natural enemies of pests
2. Soil nematodes and microbes
3. Aquatic organisms
n72ad08b5445.x: Bt toxins or other engineered traits may affect pollinators and natural enemies, soil nematodes and microbes, and aquatic organisms.

n1a5b68d59d9.s: V-GURT (terminator technology) is banned in India under which Act?
n1a5b68d59d9.x: V-GURT, which makes plants produce sterile seeds, is banned in India under the Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers' Rights Act, 2001.

n9f40fc558b3.s: Golden Rice produces which precursor of Vitamin A?
n9f40fc558b3.x: Golden Rice produces beta-carotene, using daffodil phytoene synthase and Erwinia crtI, to target Vitamin A deficiency.

n3d613be8e6b.s: Bt cotton was approved for commercial cultivation in India in:
n3d613be8e6b.x: Bt cotton was approved in March 2002 (three MAHYCO hybrids); 2006 is when Bollgard II came.

nbiology-41-3.s: In CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing, which component guides Cas9 to the desired genomic location?
nbiology-41-3.x: Guide RNA leads the Cas9 enzyme to the target site; CRISPR itself is specialised stretches of DNA.

n79f7cd5991b.s: The genome-edited Pusa Rice DST1 is tolerant to:
n79f7cd5991b.x: Pusa Rice DST1 is genome-edited for drought and salinity tolerance, giving about 10-30% higher yield under stress without foreign DNA.

na711883989a.s: A key gene-flow argument against Bt brinjal was that India is a centre of diversity of:
na711883989a.x: Transgene escape risk is highest in a crop's centre of diversity, and India is a centre of diversity of brinjal itself.

nafeeb28155c.s: In genetic medicine, engineered viruses and lipid nanoparticles serve as:
o: Probes that detect pathogens in blood
Enzymes that cut DNA at specific sites
Carriers to deliver the medicine into cells
nafeeb28155c.x: Genetic medicines, which correct or compensate for faulty genes, are delivered by engineered viruses and lipid nanoparticles.

nda5605c1a39.s: In synthetic biology, semaglutide has been grown in:
nda5605c1a39.x: Semaglutide was grown in baker's yeast; Bacillus thuringiensis is the source of Bt genes.

nbiology-40-5.s: The basic idea of gene therapy is to:
o: Change the environmental conditions of the patient
Replace damaged tissue with artificial implants
Alter, replace or correct defective genetic function
nbiology-40-5.x: Gene therapy is a genetic-engineering application that alters, replaces or corrects defective genes; it does not change the environment.

n8d454272a04.s: Bt cotton, which covers about 90% of India's cotton area, has cut pesticide use by about:
n8d454272a04.x: The cut in pesticide use is about 40-50%, not 70-80%; Bt cotton covers about 90% of the cotton area (~10.8 million ha).

nbiology-39-4.s: A recombinant plasmid is introduced into a bacterium through:
nbiology-39-4.x: The recombinant plasmid enters the bacterium by transformation, and rapid bacterial multiplication then yields large quantities of DNA or product.

nbiology-42-5.s: Copying or amplifying a desired gene or DNA fragment is called:
nbiology-42-5.x: Gene cloning copies a desired gene; whole-animal cloning copies a complete organism.

nbiology-44-4.s: The field that relates an individual's genetics to drug response is:
nbiology-44-4.x: Pharmacogenomics links genes to drug response and supports personalised or precision medicine.

nbiology-42-9.s: PCR (polymerase chain reaction) is a technique for:
o: Copying small quantities of DNA for analysis
nbiology-42-9.x: PCR copies small amounts of DNA for molecular analysis, diagnostic testing and research.

nbiology-41-5.shape: statements (one-liner not possible: every original item is correct)
nbiology-41-5.s:
Consider the following statements about CRISPR-Cas9:
1. It can be used to correct genetic defects.
2. It can be used to improve crops.
3. Its use raises ethical concerns.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
nbiology-41-5.x: CRISPR can fix genetic defects, treat or prevent disease and improve crops, and its use raises ethical concerns.

n47b2f4220d7.s: Human insulin was first marketed as Humulin in:
n47b2f4220d7.x: Humulin was marketed in 1982, after the first GMO in 1973; CRISPR-Cas9 was demonstrated in 2012.

n7d6af761a4c.s: Experiments on Bt proteins in agricultural soil have shown that they:
o: Can be removed only by burning crop residue
n7d6af761a4c.x: Although persistence of Bt proteins in soil was feared, experiments have shown that they degrade.

n326afd134d0.s: Biofortification usually raises the nutrient level of crops through:
n326afd134d0.x: Biofortification generally raises nutritional value through conventional breeding, whereas GM technology inserts foreign genes.

nbiology-43-2.s: In producing a GMO, genetic engineering transfers genes in ways that:
nbiology-43-2.x: Genetic engineering changes the genome by moving genes, often from another organism, in ways that would not happen naturally.

n4d701804137.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety?
o: It is supplementary to the Convention on Biological Diversity
It was adopted in 2000 and entered into force in 2003
It has an Advance Informed Agreement procedure for transboundary movement of LMOs
It is named after a city in Brazil
n4d701804137.x: Cartagena is in Colombia, not Brazil.

nbc01a6650e5.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Section 3(d) of the Patents Act?
o: It bars a patent for a new form of a known substance unless it shows enhanced efficacy
It is meant to block evergreening
In Novartis v Union of India (2013), the Glivec rejection was upheld under Section 3(j), not 3(d)
Section 3(j), a different clause, excludes plants, animals and seeds
nbc01a6650e5.x: The Supreme Court upheld the Glivec (imatinib) rejection under Section 3(d); Section 3(j) deals with plants, animals, seeds and essentially biological processes.

n0290ae83005.s: Which of the following is NOT listed as an environmental or health risk of GM crops?
n0290ae83005.x: Insect resistance, harm to non-target organisms, weediness, genetic homogenisation, toxicity, allergenicity and antibiotic resistance are listed risks; ozone depletion is not a GM-crop risk.

n144497fcb27.s:
Assertion (A): Under the Rules, 1989, RCGM approves the commercial release of GM crops.
Reason (R): GEAC, under MoEFCC, approves environmental release and commercial use of GM crops.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n144497fcb27.x: RCGM is under DBT and monitors ongoing research and advises GEAC; commercial approval rests with GEAC, so A is false and R is true.

nff4cbdc2dd4.s: The initial commercial approval of Bt cotton in India covered how many MAHYCO hybrids?
nff4cbdc2dd4.x: Three MAHYCO hybrids were initially approved for three years; Bt cotton remains the only GM crop commercially cultivated in India.

n545731dceb3.s: In July 2024, the Supreme Court's ruling on GM mustard DMH-11 was a:
o: Dismissal of the case as withdrawn
n545731dceb3.x: The July 2024 verdict was split, though both judges directed the Centre to frame a national GM crop policy; GEAC had cleared its environmental release in 2022.

n8ec5fa205bb.s: In the FL-2027 (FC5) potato variety case, PepsiCo sued farmers of which State?
n8ec5fa205bb.x: PepsiCo sued Gujarat farmers, later withdrew the suits, and the PPVFR Authority revoked the variety's registration in 2021.

n8296e253283.s: Which Indian law criminalises biological weapons?
n8296e253283.x: The WMD Act, 2005 criminalises biological weapons in India; India is also a Party to the BWC (opened 1972, in force 1975).

ne82c1443f70.s: The barnase-barstar genes used in GM mustard DMH-11 come from:
ne82c1443f70.x: Barnase-barstar comes from Bacillus amyloliquefaciens; Bacillus thuringiensis is the source of Bt genes. DMH-11 was developed by Delhi University.

na77208af2a0.s: Lethal agents with no cure, such as Ebola, require which biosafety level?
na77208af2a0.x: Such agents need BSL-4; BSL-2 is for moderate-risk agents and BSL-3 for serious airborne agents such as TB.

n7f239314b0f.s: Under the PPV&FR Act, 2001, farmers are NOT allowed to sell:
n7f239314b0f.x: Farmers may save, use, sow, resow, exchange, share and sell farm produce including seed, but not branded seed of protected varieties.

n382e4508f30.s: The Biotechnology Regulatory Authority of India (BRAI) Bill, 2013 proposed:
o: A ban on all GM crops
A separate patent office for seeds
A GM approval committee in every State
n382e4508f30.x: The BRAI Bill proposed a single biotechnology regulator but lapsed with the 15th Lok Sabha.

nenvironment-5-8.s: The Genetic Engineering Approval Committee was renamed the Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee in:
nenvironment-5-8.x: GEAC, constituted under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, was renamed from 'Approval' to 'Appraisal' in 2010.

n270be4621c9.s: In which year did the GEAC clear field trials of 11 crops and 21 varieties?
n270be4621c9.x: GEAC cleared these trials in 2014, after Bt cotton (2002), the PIL (2006) and the Bt brinjal moratorium (2010).

ndf05d4df4c1.s: Which body forms the first, institutional-level tier of India's biosafety system?
ndf05d4df4c1.x: The sequence begins with IBSC at institutional level, followed by RCGM, GEAC, SBCC, DLC and expert committees.

na9afc97561b.s: Approval of a GM product in India may take about 7–10 years, compared with about ____ globally.
na9afc97561b.x: Overlapping mandates of DBT, GEAC, CDSCO, FSSAI and NBA and the lack of a biosafety liability law mean 7–10 years in India against 3–5 years globally.

n8d67cad57cb.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the regulation of nanotechnology in India?
o: India has a dedicated comprehensive nano law
DGFASLI has issued guidelines on occupational risk
Dual-use concerns are addressed under the SCOMET list
n8d67cad57cb.x: India does not have a dedicated nano law; DGFASLI guidelines, FSSAI's 2022 guidelines and the SCOMET list are the relevant frameworks.

nchemistry-6-10.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Fullerene – Hollow cylinders of rolled graphene
Carbon nanotubes – Hollow cylinders of rolled graphene
Amorphous carbon – No ordered crystal lattice; mixed hybridisation
nchemistry-6-10.x: Fullerene (C₆₀) is a hollow spherical cage of 60 carbon atoms; rolled graphene cylinders are carbon nanotubes.

nchemistry-6-16.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Graphite – Transparent, with a very high refractive index
Diamond – Transparent, with a very high refractive index
Fullerene – Semiconductor with a hollow cage structure
Activated charcoal – Porous, with a very high surface area
nchemistry-6-16.x: Graphite is opaque, black and a good electrical conductor; it is diamond that is transparent and highly refractive.

na82df57fe32.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Nano Urea?
o: Its particle size is about 20–50 nm
It may reduce urea use by up to about 25%
It is applied as a foliar spray
na82df57fe32.x: Nano Urea does not fully replace conventional urea; it is a 20–50 nm foliar spray that may cut urea use by up to about 25%.

n3bbffa1dfb4.s: The Nano Mission was launched in 2007 as an umbrella programme under:
n3bbffa1dfb4.x: The Nano Mission (2007) is a DST umbrella programme, with an initial outlay of about Rs 1,000 crore for five years.

ne09aa007ad0.s: Which of the following is a bottom-up method of nanomaterial synthesis?
ne09aa007ad0.x: Self-assembly builds structures from atoms and molecules (bottom-up); lithography, milling and etching cut bulk material down (top-down).

n97f3a39467c.s: The term 'nanotechnology' was coined in 1974 by:
n97f3a39467c.x: Norio Taniguchi coined the term in 1974; Feynman's 1959 lecture gave the idea, and Iijima discovered carbon nanotubes.

n6bb3d6ae8cd.s: Which of the following is an engineered, not natural, nanoparticle?
n6bb3d6ae8cd.x: Nano-silver is deliberately manufactured; volcanic ash, sea spray and smoke are natural sources of nanoparticles.

n84a6418c2f2.s: Bawendi, Brus and Ekimov received the 2023 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for work on:
n84a6418c2f2.x: The 2023 Chemistry Nobel was for quantum dots, which show size-tunable colour and are used in displays and solar cells.

n412412ab066.s: The specification of Nano DAP was notified under the Fertiliser Control Order in:
n412412ab066.x: Nano DAP was notified under the FCO on 2 March 2023; it is used for seed treatment and foliar application.

n6950545e4b0.s: Besides quantum effects, the unusual properties of nanomaterials arise mainly from their:
n6950545e4b0.x: Quantum effects and a very high surface-area-to-volume ratio give nanomaterials enhanced reactivity and unusual optical and electrical behaviour.

nchemistry-6-5.s: Graphene is a single atom-thick, sp²-hybridised layer of:
nchemistry-6-5.x: Graphene is a one-atom-thick sp² layer of graphite; rolled graphene sheets form carbon nanotubes.

nchemistry-6-11.s: In diamond's tetrahedral network, each carbon atom is bonded to how many other carbon atoms?
nchemistry-6-11.x: Each carbon in diamond bonds to four others at the corners of a tetrahedron, giving a rigid 3D network.

n7992fa96182.s: In public health, gold nanoparticles are used for:
o: Rapid lateral-flow diagnosis of malaria, dengue and typhoid
n7992fa96182.x: Gold-nanoparticle lateral-flow kits rapidly diagnose malaria, dengue and typhoid; graphene enables bendable wearable sensors.

nf6544df0ef3.s: The indicated nitrogen-use efficiency of Nano Urea is about:
nf6544df0ef3.x: Nano Urea has an indicated nitrogen-use efficiency of about 70%, against about 30–35% for conventional urea.

nd8c1427455a.s: The third generation of nanoproducts consists of:
nd8c1427455a.x: The third generation is systems of nanosystems, including complex devices such as nanoelectronics and nanomedicine.

nc2f0fb1201e.s: The Scanning Tunnelling Microscope (STM) is used to image atoms on:
nc2f0fb1201e.x: STM images atoms on conducting surfaces, whereas the AFM can work on non-conducting materials as well.

nbiology-18-10.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Ebola – Haemorrhagic fever spread from bats and non-human primates in Africa
Nipah – Carried by fruit bats, with pigs as intermediate hosts
Fascioliasis – Viral disease of cloven-hoofed livestock
Foot-and-mouth disease – Aphthovirus disease of cloven-hoofed livestock
nbiology-18-10.x: Fascioliasis is a snail-borne liver fluke infection of cattle and sheep; the Aphthovirus disease of cloven-hoofed livestock is foot-and-mouth disease.

na3ef9d6eb23.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Wolbachia?
o: It is a Gram-negative bacterium found naturally in 40–60% of insects
It can cause cytoplasmic incompatibility, in which eggs fail to develop
It can contribute to pathogen blocking
It is naturally present in Aedes aegypti and Anopheles
na3ef9d6eb23.x: Wolbachia is naturally absent in Aedes aegypti and Anopheles.

nbiology-22-8.s: Which of the following pairs of animal disease and causative agent is wrongly matched?
nbiology-22-8.x: Cowpox is caused by the cowpox virus; Morbillivirus causes rinderpest.

n5c66e54c74b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's response to antimicrobial resistance?
o: The National Action Plan on AMR (2017) is based on the One Health approach
Kerala's KARSAP (2018) was the first State-level AMR action plan
The Red Line campaign puts a red line on the packs of all over-the-counter medicines
The Red Line campaign was launched in 2016
n5c66e54c74b.x: The Red Line (2016) marks prescription-only antibiotics, not all over-the-counter medicines.

ndce9911c126.s: Which of the following is NOT in the critical-priority group of the WHO Bacterial Priority Pathogens List, 2024?
ndce9911c126.x: The critical-priority group includes carbapenem-resistant A. baumannii, Enterobacterales and rifampicin-resistant TB; Wolbachia is not on the list.

nbiology-15-60.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Schistosomiasis – Ruminants as main hosts; raw water plants
Sleeping sickness – Tsetse fly; transmitted by bite
Amoebiasis – Humans as host; contaminated food and water
Fascioliasis – Ruminants as main hosts; raw water plants
nbiology-15-60.x: Schistosomiasis spreads through snails (intermediate hosts) in unsafe water; ruminant hosts and raw water plants describe fascioliasis.

na498d5808c5.s: Which of the following is NOT a cause or facilitating factor of antimicrobial resistance?
o: Regulated and scientifically supervised veterinary drug use
na498d5808c5.x: Overuse, self-medication and poor sanitation drive AMR; it is unregulated, not regulated and supervised, veterinary drug use that is a concern.

nbiology-15-32.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Japanese encephalitis?
o: It is caused by the Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV)
It spreads mainly through contaminated water
Pigs and wild birds are its reservoirs
nbiology-15-32.x: Japanese encephalitis spreads by mosquito bite, not through water; JEV causes it and pigs and wild birds are its reservoirs.

nbiology-15-36.s:
Assertion (A): Rinderpest no longer affects cattle and buffalo anywhere in the world.
Reason (R): Rinderpest was declared globally eradicated in 2011.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
nbiology-15-36.x: Rinderpest affected cattle and buffalo until it was declared globally eradicated in 2011, so R explains A.

nbiology-66-8.s:
Assertion (A): Not completing a course of antibiotics can promote antimicrobial resistance.
Reason (R): In an incomplete course, resistant survivors are left to multiply.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
nbiology-66-8.x: Stopping a course early lets resistant survivors multiply, which is exactly how it promotes resistance.

nced42d88767.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: only one dated event)
nced42d88767.s: The antibiotic Nafithromycin, launched in November 2024, was developed by:
nced42d88767.x: Nafithromycin was developed by Wockhardt with BIRAC support and launched on 20 November 2024 by Dr Jitendra Singh; it was not developed by Sun Pharma.

nbiology-15-25.s: Besides mosquitoes, Zika can be transmitted through:
nbiology-15-25.x: Zika virus spreads by mosquitoes, blood and sexual transmission, and causes fever, rash and joint pain.

n066f3b8fd6a.s: Scrub typhus is transmitted by the:
n066f3b8fd6a.x: Scrub typhus is spread by the chigger mite; plague by the rat flea and sleeping sickness by the tsetse fly.

nbiology-66-2.s: Which antibiotic is used to treat fungal skin infections such as ringworm?
nbiology-66-2.x: Griseofulvin treats ringworm; chloramphenicol is used for typhoid and streptomycin was the first anti-TB drug.

nbiology-16-6.s: Guinea worm larvae are carried by:
nbiology-16-6.x: Cyclops carries Guinea worm larvae; Culex spreads filariasis and JE, Anopheles malaria and Aedes albopictus dengue and chikungunya.

n079be90d1b7.s: How many of these Plasmodium species infect humans: P. falciparum, P. vivax, P. malariae, P. ovale and P. knowlesi?
n079be90d1b7.x: All five, including P. knowlesi, are recognised as infecting humans.

nbiology-15-58.x: Kala-azar attacks the liver, spleen and bone marrow; amoebiasis affects the intestine and late sleeping sickness the brain.

nb48aaf55c7a.s: About how many people are reported to live in highly climate-vulnerable areas?
nb48aaf55c7a.x: About 3.6 billion people live in highly climate-vulnerable areas, facing extreme weather and vector-borne diseases such as malaria and dengue.

nbiology-15-46.s: Which disease forms a false membrane in the throat and nose?
nbiology-15-46.x: Diphtheria forms a false membrane in the throat and nose; pertussis is whooping cough.

nbiology-15-70.s: Ergotism is caused by a toxin of:
nbiology-15-70.x: Ergotism comes from Claviceps purpurea toxin; Aspergillus causes aspergillosis and Trichophyton athlete's foot.

nbiology-18-4.x: Dracunculus medinensis causes Guinea worm disease; Ascaris causes ascariasis and Trypanosoma sleeping sickness.

nbiology-17-7.x: Taenia solium causes neurocysticercosis; Ascaris causes ascariasis and Fasciola fascioliasis.

na61614d7db9.x: Mission Indradhanush began in December 2014, targeting over 90% full immunisation of children and pregnant women.

nbiology-19-4.s: Which disease is associated with a rat–flea cycle?
nbiology-19-4.x: Plague involves a rat–flea cycle; rabies comes from dogs, cats, bats and foxes and Ebola from non-human primates.

nbiology-15-44.x: Syphilis is caused by Treponema pallidum; gonorrhoea by Neisseria gonorrhoeae and diphtheria by Corynebacterium diphtheriae.

na699f254ebf.s: Which hepatitis viruses spread through the faecal-oral route?
na699f254ebf.x: Hepatitis A and E are faecal-oral, while hepatitis B and C are generally blood-borne.

nbiology-65-13.s: Acetobacter is used in the production of:
nbiology-65-13.x: Acetobacter gives vinegar; Penicillium gives penicillin, Streptomyces streptomycin and Bacillus several antibiotics.

nbiology-63-4.x: Mycoplasma pneumoniae causes atypical pneumonia; C. tetani causes tetanus, Y. pestis plague and M. leprae leprosy.

nbiology-16-1.s: Rice tungro disease is spread by the:
nbiology-16-1.x: The leafhopper spreads rice tungro; the sandfly spreads kala-azar, the rat flea plague and the snail schistosomiasis.

nbiology-64-19.x: Leishmania donovani causes kala-azar; Entamoeba histolytica causes amoebic dysentery and Candida candidiasis.

nbiology-63-14.x: C. botulinum causes botulism; Salmonella Typhi causes typhoid and Vibrio cholerae cholera.

n7292f41085c.shape: statements (one-liner not possible: every original item is correct)
n7292f41085c.s:
Consider the following health effects:
1. Hearing loss
2. Hypertension
3. Sleep disorders and anxiety
Which of the above is/are associated with noise pollution?
n7292f41085c.x: Noise pollution is associated with hearing loss, hypertension, sleep disorders and anxiety.

n425f3d78bac.s: The adult BCG vaccination drive in Andhra Pradesh, which placed the State first in India, began on:
n425f3d78bac.x: The AP adult BCG drive began on 16 May 2024 and administered 27.10 lakh doses.

n034b4b51d06.s: In forests, yellow fever is spread by which mosquito?
n034b4b51d06.x: Forest yellow fever is spread by Haemagogus; malaria is spread by female Anopheles and Culex spreads JE and filariasis.

ne48133ae784.s: The Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897 was enacted against which disease in Bombay?
ne48133ae784.x: The four-section Act was enacted against bubonic plague in Bombay; the amendment protecting health workers came in 2020.

nbiology-17-12.x: Zika fever is caused by Zika virus; yellow fever virus causes yellow fever.

nbiology-64-7.x: Dermatophytes cause ringworm; Candida causes candidiasis, Aspergillus aspergillosis and Mucormycetes mucormycosis.

n94d7175ffb7.x: Chikungunya is caused by an alphavirus; malaria destroys red blood cells and dengue mainly affects platelets.

n3055418c098.s: The term 'antibiotic' was coined in 1942 by:
n3055418c098.x: Selman Waksman coined the term in 1942; Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928 from Penicillium notatum.

nbiology-15-45.s: Diphtheria and pertussis are transmitted mainly through the:
nbiology-15-45.x: Diphtheria and pertussis are human diseases spread through respiratory routes; gonorrhoea and syphilis are sexually transmitted.

nbiology-15-71.x: Athlete's foot affects the skin of the foot and spreads through contaminated floors, towels or clothes.

n3c47935a164.s: Rust of wheat is caused by:
n3c47935a164.x: Puccinia causes rust of wheat; Ustilago causes smut diseases.

nbiology-15-16.s: Polio, which can cause paralysis, attacks the:
o: Spinal cord and central nervous system
nbiology-15-16.x: Polio is a human viral disease spread by the faecal-oral route that attacks the spinal cord and central nervous system.

nbiology-15-17.s: COVID-19 mainly affects which system of the body?
nbiology-15-17.x: COVID-19 is a human viral disease spread by respiratory and contact routes; it attacks the lungs and can cause multi-organ complications.

nbiology-15-65.x: Neurocysticercosis comes from swallowing Taenia solium eggs, and its larvae lodge in the brain and CNS.

nbiology-66-14.s: The self-produced matrix that protects microbes in a biofilm is called:
nbiology-66-14.x: Biofilms are microbial communities in a self-made EPS matrix that protects them, raises resistance and causes chronic infections.

nbiology-43-8.s: Bacterial drug resistance graded in increasing order of severity is:
nbiology-43-8.x: Resistance is graded from multidrug-resistant (MDR) to extensively (XDR) to totally drug-resistant (TDR).

nbiology-15-61.x: Fascioliasis, caused by the liver fluke Fasciola, mainly in ruminants, is caught from raw water plants and damages the liver and bile ducts.

nbiology-15-28.s: AIDS, caused by a retrovirus, mainly destroys the:
nbiology-15-28.x: AIDS is a retroviral human disease spread through blood, sex and from mother to child, and it destroys the immune system.

nbiology-18-5.s: Pigs are an important host for which disease?
nbiology-18-5.x: Pigs host swine flu, not bird flu; rinderpest affected cattle and buffalo and plague involves a rat–flea cycle.

nbiology-15-38.x: Foot-and-mouth disease is an infectious viral disease caused by Aphthovirus, affecting cattle, goats, pigs and sheep.

nbiology-15-41.x: Leprosy, an infectious bacterial disease caused by Mycobacterium leprae, damages the skin and peripheral nerves.

nbiology-15-68.s: Ascariasis, caused by Ascaris lumbricoides, is a disease caused by a:
nbiology-15-68.x: Ascariasis is a nematode infection by Ascaris lumbricoides, caught by swallowing its eggs.

nbiology-15-35.x: Chickens host Ranikhet disease; cattle and buffalo hosted rinderpest and pigs host swine flu.

nbiology-15-31.s: Measles, a highly contagious viral disease, is transmitted mainly through:
nbiology-15-31.x: Measles is a highly contagious human viral disease spread through the air.

nbiology-20-14.x: Aspergillus flavus and A. parasiticus produce aflatoxin; Amanita mushrooms contain α-amanitin.

nbiology-20-12.s: Epidemic dropsy is caused by the oil of:
nbiology-20-12.x: Epidemic dropsy comes from mustard oil adulterated with Argemone mexicana oil, which contains sanguinarine and dihydrosanguinarine.

nbiology-15-50.s: Tuberculosis is a ____ disease transmitted through respiratory routes.
nbiology-15-50.x: Tuberculosis is a human bacterial disease spread through the air.

nbiology-66-7.shape: statements (one-liner not possible: every original item is correct)
nbiology-66-7.s:
Consider the following statements about antibiotic resistance:
1. Antibiotic use in livestock can lead to resistant strains.
2. Repeated exposure can select resistant organisms.
3. Mutation can generate resistance.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
nbiology-66-7.x: Antibiotic use in livestock, repeated exposure and mutation all contribute to resistance.

nbiology-15-10.s: Rabies, Ebola and Nipah are all:
nbiology-15-10.x: Rabies, Ebola and Nipah are viral diseases that pass from animals to humans.

nbiology-23-5.x: Morbillivirus causes rinderpest; Aphthovirus causes foot-and-mouth disease.

nbiology-19-6.s: SARS emerged from animals with which animal as an intermediate host?
nbiology-19-6.x: SARS, caused by a coronavirus, jumped to humans via civet cats as intermediate hosts.

nchemistry-15-33.x: Most antibiotics are natural or semi-synthetic and some are fully synthetic; many come from bacteria, not only fungi.

nbiology-15-21.x: Mumps is a human viral disease caused by mumps virus and spread through saliva and nasal secretions.

nbiology-15-73.s: Ergotism is associated with eating infected:
nbiology-15-73.x: Ergotism comes from eating rye or cereals infected by the ergot fungus and affects the nervous, vascular and endocrine systems.

nbiology-18-7.s: Taenia solium, which causes taeniasis and neurocysticercosis, is associated with:
nbiology-18-7.x: Taenia solium is the pork tapeworm; it infects humans, causing taeniasis and, from its eggs, neurocysticercosis.

nbiology-66-13.s: In the food industry, biofilms on food-processing surfaces chiefly cause:
nbiology-66-13.x: Biofilms cause spoilage and contamination in food plants; they are not confined to catheters.

nbiology-15-55.s: Botulinum toxin, which can cause paralysis, mainly acts on the:
nbiology-15-55.x: Botulinum toxin blocks nerves and can cause paralysis; the liver is not its target.

nbiology-15-8.x: Tetanus enters through dirty wounds, while cholera and typhoid spread through contaminated food and water.

nbiology-21-10.s: Rinderpest, now eradicated, affected which livestock?
nbiology-21-10.x: Rinderpest affected cattle and buffalo; foot-and-mouth disease affects cloven-hoofed livestock.

nbiology-15-9.s: Which disease may lead to elephantiasis by involving the lymph glands?
nbiology-15-9.x: Filarial worms block lymph vessels, causing elephantiasis; Ascaris lives mainly in the small intestine.

nbiology-43-5.shape: statements (one-liner not possible: every original item is correct)
nbiology-43-5.s:
Biofilms can form on:
1. Medical implants and human tissues
2. Food
3. Food-processing surfaces
Which of the above is/are correct?
nbiology-43-5.x: Biofilms grow on medical implants, human tissues, food and food-processing surfaces.

nb81a18e2324.s: According to the WHO figure for 2019, ambient outdoor air pollution caused about how many premature deaths?
nb81a18e2324.x: The cited WHO estimate is 4.2 million premature deaths from ambient outdoor air pollution in 2019.

n4add7b835e4.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's health transition?
o: India is undergoing a linear shift from infectious to non-communicable diseases
Life expectancy rose from 49.7 years in 1973 to 70.3 years in 2023
Maternal mortality ratio has fallen by 86% since 1990
Under-five mortality rate has risen since 1990
n4add7b835e4.x: Under-five mortality has fallen, by 78% since 1990, not risen.

nab656dc05eb.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the UN General Assembly declaration on NCDs and mental health?
o: It covers oral health, lung health and childhood cancer
It calls for relaxing the regulation of e-cigarettes
It covers air pollution and lead as determinants
It covers digital harms such as screen time
nab656dc05eb.x: The declaration calls for stronger, not relaxed, regulation of tobacco, trans fats and e-cigarettes.

nbd9e82d5d89.s:
Assertion (A): DALY is the sum of years of life lost to premature death and years of healthy life gained through treatment.
Reason (R): DALY is the sum of years of life lost (YLL) and years lived with disability (YLD).
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
nbd9e82d5d89.x: DALY = YLL + YLD; it does not add years gained through treatment, so A is false and R is true.

ne0827854765.s: Under NP-NCD (formerly NPCDCS), screening for non-communicable diseases covers everyone above:
ne0827854765.x: NP-NCD screening covers everyone over 30, not 40; it runs NCD clinics at district hospitals and CHCs.

nab3528e485d.s: Which is the leading cause of death in India?
nab3528e485d.x: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death; NCDs account for 57% of all deaths in India.

n673043878ff.s: Although cancer is not nationally notifiable, how many States have made it a notifiable disease?
n673043878ff.x: Seventeen States have notified cancer, Telangana being the most recent.

n7ad05ecda51.shape: statements (one-liner not possible: every original item is correct)
n7ad05ecda51.s:
Consider the following:
1. Unhealthy diet and physical inactivity
2. Tobacco use
3. Alcohol use
Which of the above are main risk factors for lifestyle (non-communicable) diseases?
n7ad05ecda51.x: Unhealthy diet, physical inactivity, tobacco and alcohol are all main NCD risk factors, along with urbanisation and ageing.

n43ed6e9a91b.s: Japanese encephalitis is carried by which mosquito?
n43ed6e9a91b.x: Japanese encephalitis is carried by Culex, while dengue, chikungunya and Zika are carried by Aedes.

na426921ea22.s: In the Uddanam CKDu investigation, soil, water, blood and urine samples are being tested for:
na426921ea22.x: The samples are tested for pesticides and heavy metals, with CSIR-IICT Hyderabad.

n11b91749577.s: To limit NCD risk, FSSAI caps trans fat in fats and oils at:
n11b91749577.x: Excess trans fats, common in bakery products made with hydrogenated fats, raise NCD risk, so FSSAI caps trans fat at 2%.

n7702866757b.s: In Omran's theory of epidemiological transition, the first stage is the Age of:
n7702866757b.x: Omran's sequence runs from the Age of Pestilence and Famine to Receding Pandemics and then Degenerative and Man-Made Diseases.

nbiology-70-21.s: Which of the following vaccine platforms is wrongly matched?
o: mRNA platform – Uses mRNA instructions for antigen production
Viral-vector platform – Uses a modified different virus to carry antigen instructions
Inactivated platform – Uses a genetically engineered antigen protein
Recombinant platform – Uses a genetically engineered antigen protein
nbiology-70-21.x: Inactivated vaccines use a killed pathogen; a genetically engineered antigen protein is the recombinant platform.

neaffb2f4944.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Ebola?
o: It belongs to the family Coronaviridae
The Zaire species is regarded as the deadliest
Fruit bats are identified as its reservoir
neaffb2f4944.x: Ebola belongs to the family Filoviridae, not Coronaviridae.

nbiology-73-15.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Recombinant vaccines – Antigen produced using genetic engineering
nbiology-73-15.x: Novavax is a COVID-19 recombinant protein nanoparticle vaccine; Moderna is the mRNA vaccine.

nbiology-44-3.s: Which of the following vaccine types is wrongly matched?
o: Viral vector – Vector that delivers genetic instructions
nbiology-44-3.x: A toxoid is an inactivated bacterial toxin; a weakened pathogen is a live attenuated vaccine.

n4839a4210d6.s:
Assertion (A): A major plague outbreak hit Surat, Gujarat, in 1994.
Reason (R): Plague is caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n4839a4210d6.x: Both are true: plague (Yersinia pestis) hit Surat in 1994, but naming the causative agent does not explain why the outbreak occurred there.

nbiology-71-1.s: Covaxin is based on which vaccine platform?
nbiology-71-1.x: Covaxin is an inactivated-virus vaccine; Moderna is mRNA, Sputnik V an adenovirus vector and Novavax a recombinant protein nanoparticle.

nb34904e0ffb.s: Covishield, made in India by the Serum Institute, used which platform?
nb34904e0ffb.x: Covishield was the Oxford-AstraZeneca vaccine and used an adenovirus viral-vector platform.

nc20d77d6d31.shape: statements (one-liner not possible: every original item is correct)
nc20d77d6d31.s:
Consider the following:
1. Test-track-treat-vaccinate
2. COVID-appropriate behaviour
3. MHA Empowered Groups and a three-tier facility arrangement
Which of the above formed part of India's COVID-19 strategy?
nc20d77d6d31.x: All were components of India's COVID-19 response: test-track-treat-vaccinate, COVID-appropriate behaviour, MHA Empowered Groups and a three-tier facility arrangement.

n4d6e0c0c426.s: The 'Dharavi model' ('chasing the virus') of COVID-19 containment belonged to which State?
n4d6e0c0c426.x: The Dharavi model was in Mumbai, Maharashtra; Kerala ran Break the Chain, Odisha Mo Jeeban and AP volunteer fever surveys.

n07c100c56cb.s: The MERS outbreak is associated with the year:
n07c100c56cb.x: MERS is associated with 2012 and SARS with 2002–03.

n60dc7349a77.s: The COVID-19 vaccine Corbevax was developed by:
n60dc7349a77.x: Corbevax is from Biological E, Hyderabad; Covaxin is from Bharat Biotech with ICMR-NIV and ZyCoV-D from Zydus.

n596804ad747.s: India's COVID-19 vaccination drive, guided by NEGVAC, began on:
n596804ad747.x: Vaccination began on 16 January 2021; 200 crore doses were crossed by 17 July 2022.

ncc368deb190.shape: statements (one-liner not possible: every original item is correct)
ncc368deb190.s:
Consider the following:
1. Volunteer-led fever surveys
2. Coverage under Aarogyasri
3. The Covid Pharma app
Which of the above were part of Andhra Pradesh's COVID-19 response?
ncc368deb190.x: Andhra Pradesh used volunteer fever surveys, Aarogyasri coverage for COVID treatment and the Covid Pharma app.

n821ba9d9189.s: The PMGKP insurance scheme gave health workers a cover of:
n821ba9d9189.x: PMGKP gave health workers Rs 50 lakh cover and was implemented by New India Assurance.

nbiology-71-16.s: Edward Jenner's smallpox vaccination, the first vaccination, took place in:
nbiology-71-16.x: Jenner's smallpox vaccine of 1796 was the first vaccination; Salk later made the first successful polio vaccine.

nbiology-70-11.x: DPT covers diphtheria, pertussis and tetanus; MMR covers measles, mumps and rubella.

n0e5205f555f.s: The first COVID-19 case in India was reported in Kerala on:
n0e5205f555f.x: The first case occurred on 30 January 2020; the first wave peaked in September 2020, Delta struck in April–May 2021 and Omicron in January 2022.

ne492522c153.s: The Lancet report of 24 February 2022 estimated that about how many children in India lost a parent or caregiver to COVID-19?
ne492522c153.x: The report estimated about 19 lakh children lost a parent or caregiver, not only those who lost both parents.

n2585a99d68a.s: The 2026 Bundibugyo outbreak, declared a PHEIC in May 2026, involved:
n2585a99d68a.x: The outbreak involved the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda; it was a PHEIC but not a pandemic emergency.

n3922c07fc28.s: An epidemic that spreads across countries and continents is called a(n):
n3922c07fc28.x: A pandemic spreads across countries and continents; epizootic is an epidemic among animals and endemic is constant baseline presence.

n0f766408510.s: Under PM CARES for Children, financial support is given to the child at the age of:
n0f766408510.x: The scheme covers children who lost both parents, the surviving parent or a guardian, with health insurance, education support and financial support at 23 years.

nbiology-71-23.x: Koch founded bacteriology and found the TB bacterium; rabies is Pasteur's, phagocytosis Metchnikoff's and smallpox Jenner's.

nbiology-22-6.s: In India, Nipah outbreaks have occurred in:
nbiology-22-6.x: Nipah has had outbreaks in Kerala, while COVID-19 was a pandemic.

na788fd0bb07.s: Which of the following committee–recommendation pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Mudaliar Committee – Consolidate existing PHCs and strengthen district hospitals
Kartar Singh Committee – Multipurpose health workers
Shrivastava Committee – One PHC per 50,000 people
na788fd0bb07.x: One PHC per 50,000 people was recommended by the Kartar Singh Committee (1973); Shrivastava (1975) recommended village health guides and a Referral Services Complex.

n10449487293.s: Which of the following population norms for health facilities is NOT correct?
o: Urban PHC – 25,000-30,000 people within a 10 km radius
n10449487293.x: An Urban PHC covers 25,000-30,000 people within a 2-3 km radius, not 10 km.

n87d4aaedeef.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's doctor-population ratio?
o: The ratio for NMC-registered allopathic doctors is about 1:834
It is compared with the WHO norm of 1:1000
Real availability is higher than the ratio suggests because doctors are spread evenly in rural areas
Doctors tend to cluster in cities
n87d4aaedeef.x: Real availability is lower than the ratio suggests, because doctors cluster in cities.

n5b621e69690.s:
Assertion (A): The PHC functions as a referral centre for Sub Health Centres.
Reason (R): The PHC belongs to the secondary healthcare tier.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n5b621e69690.x: The PHC is the referral centre for SHCs, but it belongs to the primary tier, not the secondary tier.

n55d9b4077f5.s: Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (earlier Health and Wellness Centres) were launched in:
n55d9b4077f5.x: They were launched in 2018; 1,50,000 HWCs were set up by December 2022 and over 1.79 lakh AAMs function in 2026.

n236aa0432e8.s: In Indian cities, which sector dominates secondary, tertiary and quaternary care?
n236aa0432e8.x: The private sector dominates higher-level care in cities, while the public system is largely curative with limited preventive care.

n5d2421cc005.s: Which of the following health committees was the earliest?
n5d2421cc005.x: Bhore (1943–46) came first, followed by Mudaliar (1959–62), Kartar Singh (1973) and Shrivastava (1975).

n40c3df7d669.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the 104 service provides:
o: Mobile medical units and health advisory
n40c3df7d669.x: 104 provides mobile medical units and health advisory services, whereas 108 is the emergency ambulance service.

n3e1621b147d.s: Which of the following is NOT correct according to the SRS abridged life tables for 2016–20?
o: Andhra Pradesh's female life expectancy was lower than India's
India's male life expectancy was 68.6 years
India's female life expectancy was 71.4 years
Andhra Pradesh's male life expectancy was 69.1 years
n3e1621b147d.x: AP's female life expectancy was 72.2 years, higher than India's 71.4 years.

n2e6fa9eb130.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about malnutrition burdens?
o: The 'double burden' is undernutrition and overnutrition occurring together
Wasting, stunting and underweight are all forms of undernutrition
SOFI 2025's 'triple burden' is wasting, stunting and underweight
A Vellore cohort study found thinness and overweight rising sharply between ages 7 and 9
n2e6fa9eb130.x: SOFI 2025's triple burden is undernutrition, micronutrient deficiency/anaemia and overweight.

n0c68ee5304b.s:
Assertion (A): Under-Five Mortality Rate (U5MR) is expressed per 1,00,000 live births.
Reason (R): Among mortality indicators, only the Maternal Mortality Ratio uses a base of 1,00,000 live births.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n0c68ee5304b.x: U5MR, like IMR, uses a base of 1,000 live births; only MMR uses 1,00,000, so A is false and R is true.

nc9b9e7b412e.s:
Assertion (A): POSHAN Abhiyaan works through convergence of ICDS, the National Health Mission and Swachh Bharat.
Reason (R): POSHAN Abhiyaan was launched in 2018 under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
nc9b9e7b412e.x: POSHAN Abhiyaan does rest on convergence of ICDS, NHM and Swachh Bharat, but it is under the Ministry of Women and Child Development.

n07a794d72b3.s: Under WHO's classification, overweight, obesity and diet-related NCDs are counted as forms of:
n07a794d72b3.x: WHO's malnutrition in all its forms covers undernutrition, inadequate vitamins and minerals, and overweight, obesity and diet-related NCDs.

nd2431dd7b23.x: NFHS-1 was in 1992-93, NFHS-2 in 1998-99, NFHS-3 in 2005-06 and NFHS-4 in 2015-16.

n924d8f85466.s: India's Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) in 2016 was:

nbiology-27-7.s: Pellagra is caused by deficiency of:
nbiology-27-7.x: Lack of B3 causes pellagra; vitamin K deficiency causes bleeding, iron deficiency anaemia and iodine deficiency goitre.

nb16ae9d30b5.s: Wasting in children refers to low:
nb16ae9d30b5.x: Wasting is low weight-for-height; stunting is low height-for-age and underweight low weight-for-age.

n21da8445614.s: According to NFHS-6, which State recorded high child wasting and underweight?
n21da8445614.x: Madhya Pradesh showed high child wasting and underweight; Meghalaya showed a decline in stunting.

nae8e0f3590e.s: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, India's life expectancy rose from 49.7 years in 1973 to how many years in 2023?
nae8e0f3590e.x: Life expectancy rose to 70.3 years in 2023; 68.3 is the older SRS 2011-15 figure and 72.2 is AP's female life expectancy for 2016-20.

n761ad9dd9a3.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA)?
o: It fixes ceiling prices of scheduled drugs
Scheduled drugs are those in the National List of Essential Medicines
Its price control operates under the Drugs Price Control Order, 2013
n761ad9dd9a3.x: NPPA was established in 1997; 2013 is the year of the Drugs Price Control Order under which it fixes ceiling prices.

nda12cb02171.s:
Assertion (A): The 15th Finance Commission's health grants include buildings for building-less SCs, PHCs and CHCs.
Reason (R): The 15th Finance Commission's health grants are intended only for urban health and wellness centres.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
nda12cb02171.x: The grants, routed through local governments, cover several components including rural and block-level infrastructure, so they are not only for urban HWCs.

n6ad66b09183.s: India's National Health Accounts, prepared by NHATS under NHSRC, use which framework?
n6ad66b09183.x: The NHA use the System of Health Accounts 2011 (with NHA Guidelines 2016); the first NHA was for 2013-14.

nd9bc64cfb6c.s: During COVID-19, household out-of-pocket expenditure fell to what share of Total Health Expenditure?
nd9bc64cfb6c.x: OOPE fell to 39.4% of THE during COVID-19, when government health expenditure peaked; 28.6% was the government share in 2013–14.

n79b4b8ba778.s: The Clinical Establishments Act, adopted by only about 11 States and 6 UTs, was enacted in:
n79b4b8ba778.x: The Act dates to 2010; 2013 is the Drugs Price Control Order and 2017 the National Health Policy.

nbbd10d8a873.s: The government share of India's Total Health Expenditure rose from 28.6% in 2013–14 to:
nbbd10d8a873.x: The government share rose to 43.7%; 39.4% is the OOPE share during COVID-19.

nc38ec89ef0a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about PM-ABHIM?
o: It focuses on health infrastructure for pandemics
It was launched on 25 October 2021 at Varanasi
Its approved outlay of ₹64,180 crore covers FY 2016–17 to FY 2020–21
It includes critical care blocks, Integrated Public Health Laboratories and BSL-3 laboratories
nc38ec89ef0a.x: The ₹64,180 crore outlay covers FY 2021–22 to FY 2025–26.

n6a708df8395.s:
Assertion (A): The Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission is implemented by the National Health Authority.
Reason (R): The Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission was launched in September 2021.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n6a708df8395.x: ABDM was launched in September 2021 and is run by NHA, but its launch date does not explain who implements it.

n22bfabe6968.s: Which of the following pairs relating to ASHA is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Level of work – Village-level community health worker
Role – Link between households and the health system
Level of work – Block-level medical officer
n22bfabe6968.x: ASHA is a village-level community health worker who, with the ANM, links rural households to the health system; she is not a block-level medical officer.

n8a81cef0c98.s: Which scheme entitles pregnant women to free ('zero expense') delivery and newborn care at public facilities?
n8a81cef0c98.x: JSSK is the free-entitlement scheme; JSY gives cash assistance for institutional delivery and is 100% centrally sponsored.

nf1cbdeb9907.s: The National Health Policy, 2017 set a life expectancy target of how many years by 2025?
nf1cbdeb9907.x: NHP 2017 aimed to raise life expectancy from 67.5 to 70 years by 2025, alongside 2.5% of GDP public spending and TFR 2.1.

n34c677c01b7.s: The Rashtriya Kishor Swasthya Karyakram (RKSK) covers adolescents aged:
n34c677c01b7.x: RKSK covers 10-19 year-olds through Adolescent Friendly Health Clinics, weekly iron folic acid supplementation and peer educators.

nd7ab6d6055e.s: Mission Indradhanush aims at what level of full immunisation?
nd7ab6d6055e.x: The December 2014 catch-up drive under UIP for zero-dose and partly immunised children targets 90% full immunisation.

n54de8bf4ddf.s: ABHA, the health ID under the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission, has how many digits?
n54de8bf4ddf.x: ABHA is a 14-digit health ID; accounts crossed 90 crore by June 2026.

nf0a68eb0b50.s: The Eat Right India campaign (2018) was launched by:
nf0a68eb0b50.x: Eat Right India is an FSSAI campaign; FSSAI was created under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

n6af44af2813.s: Along with increased public spending on health, the National Health Policy, 2002 emphasised:
o: A larger role for the private sector and NGOs
Exclusive provision of health services by the public sector
Withdrawal of the Centre from health funding
n6af44af2813.x: NHP 2002 called for more public spending and a larger role for the private sector and NGOs, not exclusive public provision.

nc135212c40e.s: Primary care, delivered through Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, is expected to meet about what share of health needs?
nc135212c40e.x: Primary care meets 80-90% of health needs; the AAM target was 1,50,000 centres and over 1.73 lakh have been converted.

n946b8d19feb.s: India's first National Health Policy was issued in:
n946b8d19feb.x: India's National Health Policies came in 1983, 2002 and 2017.

n8cfb557e619.shape: statements (NOT not possible: every original item is correct)
n8cfb557e619.s:
In Andhra Pradesh, NP-NCD additionally covers:
1. The National Mental Health Programme and elderly care
2. Iodine Deficiency Disorders and tobacco control
3. Fluorosis and oral health
Which of the above is/are correct?
n8cfb557e619.x: AP's expanded NP-NCD covers mental health, elderly care, IDD, tobacco control, fluorosis and oral health.

n5dc4a97f224.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme (NVBDCP)?
o: It handles outbreaks of malaria, dengue and chikungunya
It provides free multidrug therapy for leprosy at PHCs
It targets elimination of malaria, lymphatic filariasis and kala-azar
It deals with vector-borne diseases such as malaria and dengue
n5dc4a97f224.x: Free MDT for leprosy at PHCs is under the National Leprosy Eradication Programme (with the Sparsh campaign), not NVBDCP.

n93e7feabd40.s: Which of the following polio milestones is NOT correct?
o: India's last wild polio case was reported from Howrah in January 2011
The WHO South-East Asia Region was certified polio-free on 27 March 2014
India switched from trivalent to bivalent OPV in April 2014
Bivalent OPV covers polio types 1 and 3
n93e7feabd40.x: The switch from tOPV to bOPV took place in April 2016, not 2014.

n2f693a5e00c.s:
Assertion (A): The third '95' of the UNAIDS 95-95-95 target is a suppressed viral load in 95% of those on treatment.
Reason (R): The second '95' is that 95% of those who know their HIV status should be on treatment.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n2f693a5e00c.x: Both describe parts of the target (status, treatment, viral suppression), but the treatment goal does not explain the viral-suppression goal.

nddb8b1f7bb1.s:
Assertion (A): The National AIDS Control Programme, launched in 1992, is led by NACO under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
Reason (R): NACP Phase V (2021-26) aims at a 50% cut in new infections and AIDS deaths.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
nddb8b1f7bb1.x: A is true, but Phase V aims at an 80% cut, not 50%, so R is false.

n8f9b4421e51.s: Which of the following pairs relating to the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Access to care – Right to access mental healthcare from government services
n8f9b4421e51.x: The 2017 Act restricted ECT rather than removing restrictions on it.

ne4de4b57f80.s: In HIV services, VCTC stands for:
ne4de4b57f80.x: VCTC is the Voluntary Counselling and Testing Centre; ART is free for life at ART centres, and ICTC testing is voluntary with counselling.

n76f243e70d5.s: During 2015-2024, TB mortality in India fell by:
n76f243e70d5.x: TB mortality fell 28%, while incidence fell 21% and treatment coverage rose from 53% to 92%.

n6b75e6d6a87.s: The triple-drug IDA regimen for lymphatic filariasis uses Ivermectin, DEC and:
n6b75e6d6a87.x: IDA = Ivermectin, DEC and Albendazole; India targets LF elimination by 2027, three years ahead of the SDG target.

o: A digital portal for TB notification and tracking
An insurance scheme for TB patients
n9ab60c28d53.x: Ni-kshay is the digital TB notification and tracking portal; Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana gives nutritional DBT to all notified TB patients.

n94faf34044e.s: AVAHAN, an HIV prevention initiative in India, belongs to:
n94faf34044e.x: AVAHAN is the Gates Foundation's HIV prevention initiative, not a World Bank project; the Red Ribbon Express is an awareness train.

nbiology-19-5.s: Bivalent OPV covers which polio virus types?
nbiology-19-5.x: Bivalent OPV covers types 1 and 3, while trivalent OPV covers types 1, 2 and 3.

nc3b462e7580.s: Tele-MANAS, the tele-mental health service, was launched in:
nc3b462e7580.x: Tele-MANAS came in 2022, after the NMHP (1982), the Mental Health Act (1987) and the Mental Healthcare Act (2017).

n133bdf9b8eb.s: The Pulse Polio programme was launched in:
n133bdf9b8eb.x: Pulse Polio began in 1995, after India became smallpox-free in 1977; the last wild polio case was in 2011.

nbiology-19-7.s: Diphtheria is prevented by which type of vaccine?
nbiology-19-7.x: Diphtheria is prevented by a toxoid vaccine; hepatitis B also has a vaccine.

ca0c8735d86855.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Premier Energies' N-Type TOPCon solar cell facility?
o: TOPCon stands for Tunnel Oxide Passivated Contact
Its cells work through the photovoltaic effect
The G12R cell plant opened on 21 September 2026 has a capacity of 10.6 GW
The company's total capacity after the opening was described as India's highest
ca0c8735d86855.x: The new plant is 7 GW; 10.6 GW is the company's total capacity after the opening.

ca9127922a46c5.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about reservations for urban local bodies in Andhra Pradesh?
o: BC General mayoral posts included Eluru, Anantapur and Chittoor
Among 106 municipalities, BC General chairperson posts numbered 20
General Women reservation covered five Municipal Corporations
ca9127922a46c5.x: BC General chairperson posts numbered 18, not 20.

cae9941e0a6e96.shape: statements (NOT not possible: too few confirmed true facts)
cae9941e0a6e96.s:
Consider the following statements about Krishna river-water sharing:
1. Article 262 assigns adjudication of inter-State river disputes to Parliament.
2. The Krishna River Management Board was set up under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014.
3. One TMC-ft is approximately 28.32 billion cubic metres.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
cae9941e0a6e96.x: Article 262 gives adjudication to Parliament and the KRMB was set up under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014; one TMC-ft is about 28.32 million, not billion, cubic metres.

cac51374b09b3c.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Rayalaseema horticulture initiative?
o: It projects Andhra Pradesh as a 'fruit bowl' in place of its 'rice bowl' identity
It seeks to raise horticulture production from 222 lakh MT to 435 lakh MT
It includes 9 lakh acres of new irrigation potential
It includes stabilisation of 4.3 lakh acres
cac51374b09b3c.x: AP is projected as a fruit bowl alongside, not in place of, its rice bowl identity.

cab2999f1fa02d.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Palle Panduga 3.0?
o: It was launched on 29 September 2026 at Udayagiri in Nellore district
The Centre's share was ₹5,694 crore and the State's ₹5,391 crore
Phase 1.0 included 4,000 km of cement roads and 22,514 cattle sheds
Phase 1.0 included 21,000 farm ponds and horticulture on 64,000 acres
cab2999f1fa02d.x: The shares are reversed: the Centre's share was ₹5,391 crore and the State's ₹5,694 crore.

cafab000f8505e.s: Which of the following pairs relating to the ASUSE district data is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Highest share of women-owned enterprises in AP – Prakasam
Highest share of women workers in AP – Nandyal
Districts nationally with women-worker share above 33% – 237
cafab000f8505e.x: Nandyal, not Prakasam, had the highest share of women-owned enterprises (and of women workers and registered firms) in AP.

cac912dd2d17c3.s: The Polavaram Left Main Canal, carrying about 2 TMC per day to Uttarandhra, is planned to link Godavari with:
cac912dd2d17c3.x: The plan is to link Godavari with Vamsadhara, not Krishna.

ca23ec7ec449b2.s: As per ASUSE district data, which district had the highest number of enterprises in Andhra Pradesh?
ca23ec7ec449b2.x: Prakasam led AP in enterprises, YSR Kadapa led in workers, and Rangareddy led Telangana in enterprises.

na0abbdb399a.s: Which of the following is NOT one of Andhra Pradesh's four greenfield Other Than Major Ports (OTMPs)?
na0abbdb399a.x: Visakhapatnam is AP's only major port; the four greenfield OTMPs are Ramayapatnam, Mulapeta, Machilipatnam and Kakinada Gateway, due by end-2027.

ca0dd8ebc9de81.s: The Global Horticulture Hub–Rayalaseema Rising project covers 10 districts, 5,869 villages and how many mandals?
ca0dd8ebc9de81.x: It covers 303 mandals; 201 is the number of horticulture clusters. The project is valued at ₹1 lakh crore and covers about 9.6 lakh farmers.

cae69349ee9342.s: The Machilipatnam greenfield state port is being built by:
cae69349ee9342.x: MEIL is building Machilipatnam, while Kakinada Gateway Port is an Aurobindo Group multi-cargo facility under PPP.

ca6d878ce46ee4.s: The scientific name of the Indian gaur is:
ca6d878ce46ee4.x: The gaur is Bos gaurus; it is in WPA Schedule I, IUCN Vulnerable and CITES Appendix I.

ca3d668f4e7df1.s: The Mulapeta greenfield state port is located in which district?
ca3d668f4e7df1.x: Mulapeta is a state port in Srikakulam; Ramayapatnam is in Prakasam district.

cac162fd26ca5c.s: In cargo handled by Other Than Major Ports (OTMPs), Andhra Pradesh ranks:
cac162fd26ca5c.x: AP ranks second after Gujarat with 16% of OTMP cargo; OTMPs handle nearly 50% of India's port cargo.

cabd501eb23ebd.s: Under Component A of PM-KUSUM, decentralised grid-connected plants have a capacity of:
cabd501eb23ebd.x: Component A covers 500 kW–2 MW plants; Component C-IPS covers individual pump solarisation up to twice the pump capacity.

ca378f683fa128.s: Under Palle Panduga 3.0, the target for cement roads is:
ca378f683fa128.x: Cement roads target 6,000 km (₹2,700 crore), BT roads 9,500 km (₹7,550 crore) and Mini Gokulams 22,000 (₹300 crore).

caaba6fb0df01d.s: The Valmiki Caves near Gooty, linked to Sage Valmiki, are worshipped on:
caaba6fb0df01d.x: The caves are worshipped on Maha Shivaratri; their underground water bodies are Edu Bavulu and Gundalu.

ca43688871f484.s: Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Ltd, proposing a merchant shipyard at Dugarajapatnam, is a ____ PSU under the Ministry of Defence.
ca43688871f484.x: Mazagon Dock is a Navratna PSU; NSHIP-AP is owned equally by the AP Maritime Board and Visakhapatnam Port Authority.

caa3d9917c7f9e.s: At the meeting convened by the Union Ministry of Jal Shakti, the remaining Krishna water was to be allocated for:
caa3d9917c7f9e.x: The limited remaining water was to go to drinking and livestock needs, and crop allocation was ruled out.

ca5d54d27045b3.s: The 'Global Horticulture Hub–Rayalaseema Rising' project was launched on 2 October 2026 at:
ca5d54d27045b3.x: It was launched at Madanapalle; the foundation stone of the Indian School of Agriculture was laid the same day.

ca7b661f9f8cab.s: Along with the Danish Energy Agency and Green Power Denmark, which Indian body was part of the delegation shown Amaravati's digital twin?
ca7b661f9f8cab.x: The delegation comprised the Danish Energy Agency, Green Power Denmark and the Central Electricity Authority; the digital twin was shown at the Amaravati Integrated Command Control Centre.

ca1b3fbb8d930d.s: Oxygen isotopes in the Valmiki Caves stalagmites indicate ____ monsoons after the last Ice Age, around 11,700 years ago.
ca1b3fbb8d930d.x: The stalagmite oxygen isotopes show stronger monsoons after the last Ice Age, around 11,700 years ago.

ca6a14100d4e1f.s: Andhra Pradesh's 1,162.80 MW of feeder-level solarisation through 228 solar plants falls under which PM-KUSUM component?
ca6a14100d4e1f.x: Feeder-level solarisation is under Component C (FLS); Component B provides standalone solar pumps.

caaa96188e376a.s: Using the Q-SHIVA systems, universities can conduct up to what share of testing in-house?
caaa96188e376a.x: Universities can conduct up to 80% of testing in-house with Q-SHIVA.

cacd989d2df08f.s: A 28.95 km bituminous concrete road was completed in 24 hours on which highway?
cacd989d2df08f.x: The record was set on NH-544G; bituminous concrete is bitumen with crushed stone aggregates forming the road's upper layer.

cac23f55e84c88.s: Andhra Pradesh aims to become the maritime gateway of India's:
cac23f55e84c88.x: The aim is to be the gateway of the east coast, bridging the container gap on the Haldia–Visakhapatnam–Chennai corridor.

ca2701d39fb3f7.s: The renewable-energy investment mobilisation award was received on behalf of Andhra Pradesh by:
ca2701d39fb3f7.x: M. Kamalakar Babu received the award on behalf of NREDCAP, not the AP Pollution Control Board.
